title: Cyber Security Specialist

nodes.title: Networking Protocols & Packet Mechanics for Security
nodes.subtitle: OSI model, TCP/IP handshake, ARP spoofing, ICMP, DNS hijacking, Wireshark packet capture
learning_objectives: Analyze live network packet captures with Wireshark to identify anomalous traffic
Explain the mechanics of ARP cache poisoning and Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) attacks
feynman_prompts: How does ARP spoofing trick local network hosts into redirecting traffic to an attacker?
key_misconceptions: Assuming encrypted HTTPS traffic cannot be subjected to SNI domain inspection

nodes.title: Operating System Security & Internals
nodes.subtitle: Linux permissions, setuid, Windows access tokens, registry hives, privilege levels
learning_objectives: Audit Linux and Windows user privileges, scheduled tasks, and system services
Identify dangerous setuid binaries and weak Windows service permissions
feynman_prompts: Why does a setuid root binary represent a major privilege escalation risk if not securely written?
key_misconceptions: Running production services under administrative or root accounts without service isolation

nodes.title: Applied Cryptography: Ciphers, Hashes & PKI
nodes.subtitle: Symmetric (AES), Asymmetric (RSA, ECC), hashing (SHA-256, bcrypt), digital certificates, PKI
learning_objectives: Select appropriate cryptographic algorithms for data-at-rest and data-in-transit
Explain the Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) certificate validation chain
feynman_prompts: Why must password hashing algorithms incorporate salt and computational work factors?
key_misconceptions: Attempting to invent custom cryptographic algorithms instead of using proven industry standards

nodes.title: Reconnaissance, Port Scanning & OSINT
nodes.subtitle: Nmap scanning techniques, service versioning, NSE scripts, OSINT methodologies, Shodan
learning_objectives: Conduct stealthy network service discovery and banner grabbing using Nmap
Identify exposed enterprise assets and leaked credentials using open-source intelligence
feynman_prompts: What is the difference between a TCP SYN (half-open) scan and a full TCP connect scan in Nmap?
key_misconceptions: Scanning third-party networks without explicit legal authorization and written rules of engagement

nodes.title: Web Application Attacks: OWASP Deep Dive
nodes.subtitle: SQLi, XSS, CSRF, SSRF, Command Injection, Insecure Deserialization, XXE
learning_objectives: Exploit and remediate Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) and SQL injection flaws
Execute blind SQL injection using time-based and boolean-based payloads
feynman_prompts: How does an attacker pivot an SSRF vulnerability into cloud metadata credential theft?
key_misconceptions: Relying on client-side JavaScript input filtering to prevent web application attacks

nodes.title: Authentication, Passwords & Identity Attacks
nodes.subtitle: Credential stuffing, brute-forcing with Hydra, password spraying, MFA bypass methods
learning_objectives: Test authentication endpoints against credential stuffing and brute-force attacks
Analyze the security trade-offs of SMS vs TOTP vs FIDO2 WebAuthn authentication
feynman_prompts: Why is FIDO2 WebAuthn resistant to phishing attacks while TOTP authenticator apps are not?
key_misconceptions: Assuming account lockout policies prevent brute-force attacks without considering password spraying

nodes.title: Network Defense: Next-Gen Firewalls & IDS/IPS
nodes.subtitle: Stateful inspection, Snort / Suricata rule authoring, signature vs anomaly detection
learning_objectives: Author custom Suricata/Snort detection rules to identify malicious payload patterns
Configure stateful packet filtering and demilitarized zones (DMZ)
feynman_prompts: What is the operational difference between an Intrusion Detection System (IDS) and an IPS?
key_misconceptions: Relying exclusively on signature detection for zero-day and polymorphic attack vectors

nodes.title: Endpoint Detection, Response (EDR) & Sysmon
nodes.subtitle: EDR agents, Windows Sysmon logging, Process creation (Event 1), LOLBins, parent-child process analysis
learning_objectives: Configure Windows Sysmon to log critical process creation and network connection events
Identify Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBins) used for stealthy execution
feynman_prompts: How do security analysts use parent-child process relationships (e.g. Word spawning powershell.exe) to detect attacks?
key_misconceptions: Disabling endpoint monitoring because antivirus is already installed

nodes.title: Security Operations & SIEM Log Analysis
nodes.subtitle: Splunk, ELK, log parsing, correlation rules, alert triage, false positive reduction
learning_objectives: Build correlation searches in Splunk/ELK to detect multi-stage cyber attacks
Execute structured Tier-1/Tier-2 SOC alert triage and document incident tickets
feynman_prompts: Why is log normalization and correlation critical when analyzing telemetry from 50 disparate tools?
key_misconceptions: Setting up un-tuned SIEM alerts that flood analysts with thousands of false positives daily

nodes.title: Privilege Escalation: Linux & Windows
nodes.subtitle: LinPEAS, WinPEAS, kernel exploits, SUID abuse, token impersonation, potato attacks
learning_objectives: Identify and exploit misconfigured sudo permissions and vulnerable SUID binaries on Linux
Execute Windows privilege escalation using unquoted service paths and token manipulation
feynman_prompts: Explain how an unquoted Windows service path with spaces can allow an attacker to gain SYSTEM privileges.
key_misconceptions: Assuming low-privilege service account compromise cannot be escalated to full domain control

nodes.title: Active Directory Attacks & Defense
nodes.subtitle: Kerberos authentication, Kerberoasting, AS-REP roasting, BloodHound, Pass-the-Hash
learning_objectives: Map Active Directory attack paths and Domain Admin escalation routes using BloodHound
Execute and defend against Kerberoasting attacks targeting service accounts
feynman_prompts: Explain how Kerberoasting extracts service account password hashes without touching target servers.
key_misconceptions: Using short, simple passwords for Active Directory service accounts with Service Principal Names

nodes.title: Malware Analysis Fundamentals & Sandboxing
nodes.subtitle: Static analysis with Strings/PEStudio, dynamic analysis in sandboxes, disassembly basics
learning_objectives: Extract indicator of compromise (IOC) strings and imported APIs from suspicious binaries
Execute behavioral malware analysis in isolated sandboxes while monitoring network beacons
feynman_prompts: What is the difference between static malware analysis and dynamic behavioral analysis?
key_misconceptions: Detonating suspicious files on production or corporate workstations instead of isolated labs

nodes.title: Threat Hunting & MITRE ATT&CK Framework
nodes.subtitle: MITRE ATT&CK matrix, cyber kill chain, hypothesis-driven threat hunting, threat intelligence
learning_objectives: Map observed adversary tactics and techniques directly to the MITRE ATT&CK framework
Execute hypothesis-driven threat hunts across enterprise telemetry to uncover stealthy persistence
feynman_prompts: Why is hypothesis-driven threat hunting necessary when automated alert rules detect zero anomalies?
key_misconceptions: Focusing only on indicators of compromise (hashes/IPs) instead of adversary TTPs (tactics, techniques, procedures)

nodes.title: Cloud Security Architecture & Identity Attacks
nodes.subtitle: AWS IAM policies, metadata service (IMDSv2), Azure AD, cloud privilege escalation
learning_objectives: Enforce IMDSv2 across cloud workloads to prevent SSRF cloud credential theft
Audit cloud tenant permissions for external guest access and excessive wildcard permissions
feynman_prompts: How does IMDSv2 mitigate SSRF attacks that exploit AWS instance metadata endpoints?
key_misconceptions: Allowing IMDSv1 on cloud instances where web application services are deployed

nodes.title: Digital Forensics & Incident Response (DFIR)
nodes.subtitle: Live response, volatility memory analysis, disk imaging, evidence chain of custody
learning_objectives: Capture volatile system RAM before shutting down compromised endpoints
Maintain strict legal chain of custody for digital evidence during forensic investigations
feynman_prompts: Why must volatile system memory be dumped before pulling the power cord on a compromised server?
key_misconceptions: Modifying or browsing files directly on an original compromised forensic evidence disk

nodes.title: Penetration Testing Methodologies & Reporting
nodes.subtitle: Scope definition, rules of engagement, vulnerability exploitation, executive reporting
learning_objectives: Execute structured penetration testing adhering to PTES and OWASP testing standards
Author clear executive summaries and actionable technical remediation reports for clients
feynman_prompts: Why is an actionable remediation section more valuable to an executive than a list of exploits?
key_misconceptions: Delivering automated vulnerability scanner output as a finalized penetration testing report

nodes.title: Security Governance, Risk & Compliance (GRC)
nodes.subtitle: NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF), risk matrices, vulnerability risk assessments, policies
learning_objectives: Assess organizational cybersecurity posture using the NIST CSF framework
Calculate risk impact and likelihood using structured risk assessment matrices
feynman_prompts: What are the five core functions of the NIST Cybersecurity Framework (Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover)?
key_misconceptions: Viewing security compliance checklists as equivalent to operational cybersecurity resilience

nodes.title: Security Orchestration, Automation & Response (SOAR)
nodes.subtitle: SOAR playbooks, automated IP blocking, webhook integrations, automated incident triage
learning_objectives: Design automated SOAR playbooks that ingest alerts and quarantine infected endpoints instantly
Integrate threat intelligence feeds into automated SIEM enrichment workflows
feynman_prompts: How does SOAR automation reduce mean time to respond (MTTR) from hours to seconds?
key_misconceptions: Automating destructive isolation actions without human-in-the-loop approval for critical domain controllers

description: Master Cyber Security Specialist with an industry-standard, comprehensive curriculum spanning 18 core and advanced milestones.
